briefs.title: Keep Claude Code’s cache warm for an hour
briefs.takeaway: API-key sessions and all subagents cache for 5 minutes. One setting makes it an hour.

snippets.intro: Needs Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

notes: `promptCacheTtl` covers the main conversation. `subagentPromptCacheTtl` covers subagents, compaction and other background requests.
On a Claude subscription, within your plan’s usage, the main conversation already gets a 1-hour cache. With an API key or a cloud provider it gets 5 minutes.
1-hour cache writes bill at 2x base input, against 1.25x for 5 minutes. It pays off when you often idle past five minutes.
Same thing as env vars: `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h`.

briefs.title: Run parallel agents without overwriting each other
briefs.takeaway: Two sessions in one folder share one working copy. Give each session its own worktree.

snippets.intro: `claude --worktree auth` creates `.claude/worktrees/auth/` on a new branch named `worktree-auth`.
Copies gitignored files into every new worktree:
Gives a subagent its own worktree every time:

notes: A subagent’s temporary worktree is removed automatically if it finishes without changes.
Add `.claude/worktrees/` to your `.gitignore`.
New worktrees branch from your default branch. Set `"worktree": {"baseRef": "head"}` in settings.json to branch from your current work instead.

briefs.title: Your Claude Code session isn't empty
briefs.takeaway: CLAUDE.md, auto memory, MCP tool names and skill descriptions load before you type. Check `/context`.

snippets.intro: Before you blame the model, check what is already in context:
Keep a skill you only run yourself out of context:

notes: Only your user and project CLAUDE.md load at session start. CLAUDE.md files in subfolders load when Claude works there.
MCP tool names and server instructions load at start; full tool schemas stay deferred until a tool is used.
The 7,850-token figure in the video is the docs’ illustrative example session. Your numbers depend on your setup.

briefs.title: Claude Code’s “Don’t ask again” writes a file
briefs.takeaway: Each “Yes, and don’t ask again” becomes an allow rule in `.claude/settings.local.json` at the repo root.

snippets.intro: Created the file by hand? Ignore it yourself:

notes: The rule applies to every session in the repo, including subdirectories and worktrees.
The first time Claude Code writes the file in a repo that doesn’t already ignore it, it adds `**/.claude/settings.local.json` to your global git excludes.
Rules are plain command text. Keep tokens out of commands you approve for good.
Run `/permissions` to see every rule and the settings file it came from.

briefs.title: A rule in CLAUDE.md isn’t a rule
briefs.takeaway: CLAUDE.md is context Claude tries to follow. A PreToolUse hook blocks the action, in every permission mode.

snippets.intro: Run a check before every Bash command:
Save it and run `chmod +x` on it. Exit 2 blocks the call and sends your message to Claude.

notes: Exit 0 hands the call to the normal permission flow.
The script needs jq installed. Without it, it exits 0 and blocks nothing.
The grep matches that exact text only, so extend it for variants like `rm -fr`.
A hook’s block holds in every permission mode, including bypassPermissions.

briefs.title: Subagents save context, not usage
briefs.takeaway: A subagent keeps your context clean, but its requests count toward the same usage limits. Give simple ones a cheaper model.

snippets.intro: Give a simple subagent a cheaper model:
Or force one model onto every subagent. Needs Claude Code v2.1.257 or later.

notes: With `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` on, the `model` field in each subagent is ignored. Forks still run on your main conversation’s model.
Run `/tasks` while a subagent works to see which model it runs on.
On a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise plan, `/usage` shows the share of your usage that went to subagents.
The 420 and 9,890 token counts in the video are the docs’ illustrative example session. Agent teams in plan mode use about 7x the tokens of a standard session.

briefs.title: /loop is for this session, not next week
briefs.takeaway: `/loop` turns a prompt into a cron job that lives inside your current session. For schedules that outlast it, use a Desktop or cloud scheduled task.

snippets.intro: The first runs every 4m 45s. The second lets Claude pick each wait, between 1 minute and 1 hour.

notes: The video says recurring tasks expire after 7 days. Since Claude Code v2.1.330 they run up to 30 days, fire one last time, then delete themselves. Tasks created on older versions keep the 7-day limit.
`Esc` and `Ctrl+C` don’t stop a fixed-interval loop. Ask Claude to cancel it, for example “cancel the deploy check loop”.
Tasks fire only while Claude Code is running and idle. A run that comes due while Claude is busy fires once when it’s free, with no catch-up.
Hourly and daily tasks start 0 to 30 minutes late, by the same amount every run. A `*/5` task starts 15 seconds early instead, before the 5-minute prompt cache expires.
Closing the terminal stops the loop. Backgrounding the session keeps it running without one.
A Desktop scheduled task runs on your machine with no open session. A cloud scheduled task runs with your machine off, at most once an hour.

briefs.title: Keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines
briefs.takeaway: Longer CLAUDE.md files cost more context and reduce adherence. Keep every-session facts, and move the rest to path-scoped rules and skills.

snippets.intro: Move folder-specific rules into a path-scoped rule. It loads only when Claude reads or edits a matching file.
Check how long your instruction files are:

notes: `/init` writes a starting CLAUDE.md. If one already exists, it suggests improvements instead of overwriting it.
Keep CLAUDE.md to facts Claude needs every session: build commands, conventions, project layout and “always do X” rules.
`@path` imports organize a long file but don’t reduce its context cost. Imported files load with the CLAUDE.md that imports them.
Turn multi-step procedures into skills. A skill’s body loads only when it’s used.

If two instructions contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily. `/doctor prompt-audit` (Claude Code v2.1.283 or later) reports conflicts with proposed edits and changes nothing until you ask.

briefs.title: Claude Code’s /fast has a hidden cost
briefs.takeaway: Fast mode is up to 2.5x faster at 2x the price per token. Turn it on at the start of a session: mid-conversation, the next request rereads everything uncached at the fast rate.

snippets.intro: Turn it on at the start of a session, not mid-way:
Make every session start with fast mode off:

notes: Fast mode prices per million input / output tokens: $8 / $40 on Opus 5.5, $16 / $80 on Fable 5.2, $10 / $50 on Opus 5 and Opus 4.8. That is 2x each model’s standard rate.
On a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise plan, fast mode bills usage credits only, even with plan usage left. Usage credits must be on, and Team and Enterprise need an Owner to enable fast mode.
Fast and standard speed keep separate caches. Each later toggle rereads uncached whatever the other speed hasn’t cached, including Claude Code’s own fallback to standard speed after a rate limit.

The $1.20 and $0.06 in the video are API list prices for one 150,000-token read on Opus 5.5: at least $8 per million uncached (a cache write costs more), 0.05x that as a cache hit. Across a whole session, fast mode from the start also pays 2x on every earlier turn.
Fast mode for Opus 4.8 is removed on November 30, 2026. Opus 5.5 needs Claude Code v2.1.280 or later.
